prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Baytown, Texas. Injury: whiplash. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1083; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name in the transcript, so you can just refer to me as the plaintiff.

Q: Fine. Let's begin with the collision itself. Where were you when it happened?
A: I was in a parking lot in Baytown, Texas, pulling into a space near the store entrance.

Q: Were you moving or stopped at the time of impact?
A: I was moving slowly, maybe walking speed, looking for an open spot. Then a vehicle backed into the driver's side of my car.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle before it hit you?
A: No. I heard a horn and then felt the jolt. My head snapped forward and then back against the headrest.

Q: Did you get out of your vehicle at the scene?
A: Yes, but I felt unsteady and sat down on the curb for a while. Someone at the store brought me water.

Q: When did you first notice pain in your neck?
A: That evening. I figured it was just stiffness from the jolt, but by the next morning I couldn't turn my head to the left without sharp pain.

Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic the following day. They diagnosed whiplash and gave me a soft collar and muscle relaxers.

Q: Have you continued treatment since then?
A: I've had physical therapy twice a week for several months. I also saw a chiropractor for a while, but I stopped that after a few visits because it didn't help much.

Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: It's hard to drive for long stretches. I used to coach my nephew's soccer team on weekends, and I had to hand that over to my brother. Sleeping is also difficult because I wake up with pain in my upper back.

Q: Have you missed any work?
A: I've taken some sick days and worked a modified schedule for a few weeks. My job involves a lot of lifting, so I was restricted from heavy tasks for a while.

Q: Do you have any prior neck or back problems?
A: I had some mild neck stiffness years ago after a long desk job, but nothing that required a doctor or time off.
